title: Reduce perf-canary variance via warmup + cache priming; add noise budget report
author: Marcus Reed
description:
Problem: the current canary time-series for p95 latency and tokens/sec is too noisy to support tight regression thresholds, especially right after deploys and node rotations. The biggest contributors we’ve observed in us-east phase-1 are (a) cold-start effects (model load, kernel/autotune, allocator/JIT), (b) cache effects (KV cache and page cache), and (c) occasional node-level contention causing outliers that dominate p95 when sample counts are small.

This PR introduces two variance-reduction mechanisms and a lightweight “noise budget” report so we can quantify stability (and avoid accidentally hiding real regressions):

1) Warmup phase (excluded from regression metrics)
- Adds an explicit warmup stage per (region, model, workload-shape) before entering the measurement window.
- Warmup issues a small number of requests (configurable) to pay one-time costs (model init, kernel selection/autotune where applicable).
- Warmup requests are tagged with run_phase=warmup and excluded from the perf regression metrics stream (but still recorded in logs/traces for debugging).
- Rationale: reduce post-deploy spikes and prevent “first 5 minutes after a rollout” from constantly paging.

2) Cache priming step (controlled and bounded)
- Adds an optional cache priming step immediately before each measurement window.
- Priming uses a deterministic prefix for the prompt set (per model family) so we get repeatable cache behavior, and it is bounded by max_tokens and request_count.
- Priming requests are tagged run_phase=prime and excluded from regression metrics.
- Rationale: tokens/sec was showing large swings based on whether we happened to hit a cold KV/page cache on that runner node.

3) Noise budget report (new stability telemetry)
- Adds a per-slice “noise budget” computation emitted once per window, intended to answer: “Is this signal stable enough to page on?”
- Report fields include: sample_count, outlier_drop_count, p50/p95, coefficient_of_variation (throughput), p95_to_median_ratio, and a recommended_min_samples based on observed dispersion.
- Emitted as structured log line and as a compact metric (bucketed ratios, not raw distributions) to avoid cardinality blowups.
- This will be used by ENG-2846 detector logic to gate paging when the signal is unstable (follow-up will wire it into suppression logic; this PR only emits the report).

Trade-offs / caveats
- Warmup/priming can hide regressions that only occur from a cold state. To address this, we keep warmup/priming traces and also add an optional “cold_start_probe” mode (disabled by default) that runs a single cold request per window and records it separately (not used for paging).
- Added traffic: warmup+priming increases canary request volume. Defaults are conservative (warmup_requests=2, prime_requests=1) and rate limited. All traffic uses the canary-safe request class and existing per-runner QPS caps.
- Baseline comparability: because warmup/prime are excluded from regression metrics, the measured windows should become more comparable across deploys; however, existing historical baselines may shift slightly. Expect ~5–15% reduction in variance on tokens/sec based on initial backtests.

Implementation notes
- New config knobs:
  - warmup.enabled, warmup.request_count, warmup.max_tokens
  - prime.enabled, prime.request_count, prime.max_tokens
  - noise_budget.enabled
  - cold_start_probe.enabled
- Runner changes:
  - Run phases: warmup -> prime -> measure (-> optional cold_start_probe)
  - Phase tags are propagated via request metadata and trace attributes.
- Metrics changes:
  - Regression metrics now explicitly filter run_phase=measure.
  - Added noise_budget.* metrics with strict label set (model, region, gpu_sku, streaming) and bucketed values.

Testing
- Unit tests for phase transitions, config parsing, and deterministic prompt prefix selection.
- Integration test verifies that warmup/prime requests do not contribute to p95/tokens_sec time-series (ensures filter is applied at emission).

Rollout plan
- Merge behind config flags. Default warmup+prime enabled for phase-1 runners in us-east only.
- After 48h of observation, we’ll tune request_count and thresholds with SRE (Tomáš/Sean) and decide whether to enable in eu-west.

Screenshots/notes
- Included example noise budget output in the PR conversation. Early test run: tokens/sec CoV dropped from ~0.22 to ~0.09 on llama-3.1-70b (streaming) under pinned scheduler mode.

Refs: ENG-2852 (Noise reduction), ENG-2842 (workload matrix), ENG-2846 (detector logic will consume noise budget).

review_conversation: Noah Patel: Warmup/priming makes sense, but I want to ensure we’re not masking a class of regressions that show up on cold nodes right after a deploy. Can we keep a separate cold-start signal somewhere?

Marcus Reed (author): Yep. Added cold_start_probe (disabled by default) that runs a single cold request per window and logs/ traces it with run_phase=cold_probe. Not included in paging metrics, but should be visible for investigation.
Logan Wright: Please be very careful about noise_budget metric labels. We can’t add high-cardinality fields here (prompt_set_id, runner_id, etc). What’s the exact label schema?

Marcus Reed (author): Agree. Noise budget metrics only include: model, region, gpu_sku, streaming, scheduler_mode (already allowed). Values are bucketed ratios (e.g., cov_bucket, p95_ratio_bucket) so we don’t create a new histogram explosion.
Nadia Rahman: How are we guaranteeing warmup/prime requests are excluded from the p95 and tokens/sec metrics? Is it a filter at the runner, or a downstream query filter?
Marcus Reed (author): Filter at emission: regression series only emits when run_phase=measure. Also added an integration test that runs warmup+measure and asserts only measure requests are counted.
Sofia Ivanova: Any interaction with scheduler pinning? If warmup uses different parameters than measure, we might warm up the wrong codepath.
Marcus Reed (author): Warmup uses the same scheduler pinning and the same streaming/non-streaming mode as measure for that workload slice. Only differs in max_tokens/request_count to keep it bounded.
Tomáš Novák: Can we add a note in docs that warmup/priming increases traffic and should be kept low during regional incidents/maintenance windows?
Marcus Reed (author): Added docs/runner-variance.md section “Operational considerations” with recommended caps and how to disable warmup+prime via config quickly.
Noah Patel: Approved with the condition that cold_start_probe remains clearly separated from paging logic and that we document the trade-off explicitly.
Marcus Reed (author): Done. Documented in description + docs; cold_start_probe disabled by default.
release_notes: perf-canary runner: add optional warmup + cache priming phases (excluded from regression metrics) and emit a per-window noise budget report to quantify signal stability.
